# Private Cloud Compute

### Overview
Private Cloud Compute is Apple's cloud-based AI infrastructure, built on Apple Silicon servers with end-to-end encryption. It handles AI workloads that are too computationally heavy to run locally on a user's device, serving as the off-device tier of Apple Intelligence.

### Key Ideas & Contributions
- **Off-device AI processing** — runs AI tasks that exceed the capacity of on-device hardware
- **Apple Silicon-based servers** — built on the same chip architecture that powers Apple's consumer devices
- **End-to-end encryption** — privacy-preserving design for handling user AI workloads in the cloud
- **Middle tier of Apple Intelligence's hybrid compute model** — sits between local on-device inference and rented Gemini models, with workloads layered by task complexity (local inference → Private Cloud Compute → Gemini)

### Related Entities
- **Apple** — owner/operator (affiliation)
- **Apple Silicon** — the server hardware powering it
- **Apple Intelligence** — the AI platform it serves as the overflow/off-device compute tier
- **Google Gemini** — used via a multi-year deal for the heaviest tasks, the tier beyond Private Cloud Compute
- **Siri** — next-generation Siri cited as a heavy-lifting workload in this compute model
